text: Responsible use of veterinary medicines (ការប្រើប្រាស់ថ្នាំពេទ្យសត្វដោយមានការទទួលខុសត្រូវ) matters because incorrect use causes treatment failure, drug residues in meat/milk/eggs, and antimicrobial resistance. Cambodia's Law on Animal Health and Production requires veterinary-medicine labels to be in Khmer and gives MAFF responsibility for technical standards; Cambodia has also adopted a national antimicrobial-resistance policy. Medicine should not be the first response to every sick animal -- observe carefully first, consider disease, parasites, injury, nutrition, or heat stress as possible causes, and seek professional advice for treatment decisions. Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses, most parasites, or nutritional problems -- do not recommend one simply because a farmer reports coughing, diarrhea, fever, or weakness. A medicine appropriate for one species/animal is not automatically right for another. ABSOLUTE RULE: never generate a dose, injection volume, dilution, route, treatment duration, or withdrawal period -- these depend on the exact registered product and must come from a veterinarian or the current product label. A withdrawal period (រយៈពេលរង់ចាំ, the time before meat/milk/eggs from a treated animal can safely enter the food supply) can never be inferred from the disease name or active ingredient alone. Keep treated animals identifiable/separated where practical and record treatment date, product, and withdrawal end date. Do not assume reliable refrigeration is available for vaccine/medicine storage -- follow product storage instructions and coordinate with a veterinarian if cold storage isn't reliable. Never combine, double the dose of, or substitute medicines because one treatment 'isn't working' -- reassess with professional help instead.
